endorsements.quote: Second, mandatory subgroup reporting requires performance metrics should be disaggregated by relevant demographic subgroups, rather than reported only at the population level.

Third, intended-use scoping dictating that any synthetic dataset should document the specific purpose for which it was validated, consistent with the fit-for-purpose principle illustrated in Figure 1 .

Third, privacy validation applies adversary-aware tests, including membership inference attacks (which test whether an adversary can identify individuals from the training set) and attribute inference evaluation (which tests whether sensitive attributes can be reconstructed), rather than relying on the absence of direct identifiers alone.

unlisted_practices: Require mandatory three-layer validation (fidelity, utility, and privacy) for any publication using synthetic cardiology data.
Validate synthetic data utility using a train-on-synthetic, test-on-real paradigm for the downstream task.

Cardiology societies and regulatory agencies should define domain-specific acceptability thresholds for synthetic evidence, starting with lower-stakes applications before higher-stakes regulatory submissions.
Validate findings derived from synthetic data on real-world data before using them to support regulatory decisions.
Choose the synthetic data generation model to fit the intended use case before validation.
Researchers and sponsors should document synthetic datasets against intended-use scope, fidelity thresholds, privacy testing, and real-data validation criteria to support transparency.
Distinguish synthetic data used as a privacy-preserving distributional substitute from synthetic data used as a counterfactual simulation tool and apply validation criteria appropriate to each role.
Use deliberate methodological choices such as stratified sampling, conditional generation targeting underrepresented groups, and rigorous subgroup validation to achieve diversity in synthetic data.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint article presenting recommendations and governance frameworks for the use of synthetic data in cardiology research and AI development.
